subject: french
promptStrong: Give me a 40-word writing task in French on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer for accuracy and range.
promptWeak: Give me a two-way translation drill (French↔English) on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, with answers and the common mistakes to avoid.

questions.q: How do you say 'I get on well with my sister'?
options: Je m'entends bien avec ma sœur
Je me dispute avec ma sœur
questions.explain: 'S'entendre bien avec' means 'to get on well with', so 'Je m'entends bien avec ma sœur' = 'I get on well with my sister'.

questions.q: What does 'mon frère aîné' mean?
questions.explain: 'Aîné' means 'elder/older', so 'mon frère aîné' = 'my older brother'. 'Cadet' would mean younger.

questions.q: How would you write 'gentil' to describe a woman (kind)?
questions.explain: The feminine singular of 'gentil' doubles the l and adds -e: 'gentille'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'My parents are divorced'?
questions.explain: 'Divorcé' = divorced; 'marié' = married and 'fiancé' = engaged are near-miss distractors.

questions.q: What does 'On peut compter sur lui' mean?
questions.explain: 'Compter sur' means 'to rely/count on', so 'On peut compter sur lui' = 'You can rely on him'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I have brown hair and blue eyes'?
options: J'ai les cheveux bruns et les yeux bleus
Je suis les cheveux bruns et les yeux bleus
J'ai les cheveux bleus et les yeux bruns
J'ai le cheveux brun et les yeux bleu
questions.explain: Use 'avoir' for features and make adjectives agree (plural): 'les cheveux bruns', 'les yeux bleus'.

questions.q: What does 'mener une vie saine' mean?
questions.explain: 'Sain/saine' means 'healthy', so 'mener une vie saine' = 'to lead a healthy life'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'You must avoid fatty foods'?
options: Il faut éviter les aliments gras
Il faut manger les aliments gras
On doit boire les aliments gras
questions.explain: 'Il faut' = 'one must' and 'éviter' = 'to avoid', so this means 'You must avoid fatty foods'.

questions.q: What does 'le tabagisme' mean?
questions.explain: 'Le tabagisme' is the habit/addiction of smoking; a tobacconist's is 'le bureau de tabac'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I exercise to keep fit'?
options: Je fais de l'exercice pour rester en forme
Je fais de l'exercice pour grossir
Je fais de l'exercice parce que je suis en forme
Il fait de l'exercice pour rester en forme
questions.explain: 'Rester en forme' = 'to keep fit' and 'pour' = 'in order to'; 'je fais' is the correct first-person form.

questions.q: What does 'le bien-être' mean?
questions.explain: 'Le bien-être' literally means 'being well' and translates as 'wellbeing'.

questions.q: What does 'passer un examen' mean?
questions.explain: Classic false friend: 'passer un examen' means 'to sit/take an exam', not to pass. 'To pass' is 'réussir un examen'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'I have to revise for my exams'?
options: Je dois réviser pour mes examens
questions.explain: 'Réviser' = 'to revise' and 'devoir' = 'to have to', so 'Je dois réviser pour mes examens' = 'I have to revise for my exams'.

questions.q: What does 'une matière' mean (at school)?
questions.explain: In a school context 'une matière' means 'a (school) subject', e.g. 'ma matière préférée' = 'my favourite subject'.

questions.q: How do you say 'I would like to be a nurse'?
questions.explain: 'Je voudrais' (conditional) = 'I would like' and 'infirmier' = 'nurse'; 'malade' means 'ill', a near-miss distractor.

questions.q: What does 'le chômage' mean?
questions.explain: 'Le chômage' means 'unemployment'; someone unemployed is 'au chômage'.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'Yesterday I worked a lot' (past)?
questions.explain: 'J'ai travaillé' is the perfect tense (completed past) 'I worked'; with 'hier' (yesterday) the perfect is correct.

questions.q: How would you write 'sportif' to describe a sporty woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -if change to -ive in the feminine singular, so a sporty woman is 'sportive'.

questions.q: Which means 'I am tired' (right now)?
questions.explain: 'Je suis fatigué' = 'I am tired'. 'Fatigant' means 'tiring', a near-miss distractor.

questions.q: What does 'Je suis sensible' mean?
questions.explain: False friend: 'sensible' in French means 'sensitive'. 'Sensible' (English) would be 'raisonnable'.
